recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group later decides XML canonicalization cannot safely guarantee primitive-value whitespace preservation, handle that through the unresolved R6 signature rewrite/canonicalization trackers rather than by restoring the obsolete 2019 warning text here.
issue_request: FHIR-18441 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core XML after STU3. It asked whether XML digital-signature canonicalization that normalized whitespace to single spaces could subtly change meaning, especially for markdown serialized in XML attributes, and its final resolution called for warning about this normalization risk.
initial_application: Git commit 543388f9fe1aa2f08a988c3cc888ddd622085376 originally applied the issue by adding warning notes to source/datatypes.html and source/xml.html. Jira also records that the change was committed to both the R4 technical correction and current build.
additional_context: The current build centralizes signature details in source/signatures.html, which is active under Security and Privacy. source/xml.html#digsig links to signatures.html#xml, and source/datatypes.html#Signature points readers to the signatures page. Later signature-page refactors removed the old warning text but replaced the risky behavior with an explicit rule that whitespace in non-XHTML primitive values SHALL not be altered, including multiple spaces in markdown. The linked Zulip thread supports the original concern, and no later final Jira or Confluence evidence was found requiring duplicate warning text.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active rule directly prevents the markdown whitespace normalization problem, and adding separate prose to xml.html or datatypes.html would duplicate the centralized signatures guidance.
